title: The 3-Second Silence FBI Interrogators Use

scenes.caption: FBI behavioral interrogators know that suspects rarely break from aggressive shouting — they break from deliberate, unbroken silence.
scenes.caption_roman: FBI behavioral interrogators know that suspects rarely break from aggressive shouting — they break from deliberate, unbroken silence.

scenes.caption: When an agent maintains eye contact and stays silent for three full seconds after an answer, social anxiety spikes exponentially.
scenes.caption_roman: When an agent maintains eye contact and stays silent for three full seconds after an answer, social anxiety spikes exponentially.

scenes.caption: Behavioral scientists call this verbal leakage. The human brain interprets silence as suspicion and feels compelled to fill the void.

scenes.caption: Statement analysis proves: innocent people give short, direct answers. Deceptive suspects add unnecessary justifications and alibi padding.
